40885848.exclusion_reason: Narrative review of infant brain MRI studies on neural circuitry/psychopathology risk; 'neural network' refers to brain circuits, not an AI/ML model.

40913670.clinical_problem: Assessing adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (Cobb angle, curve type, curve direction) without ionizing radiation
40913670.model_description: Multi-task deep learning model takes structured back-surface data from fringe-projection 3D imaging as input and jointly predicts Cobb angle, curve type, and curve direction.
40913670.headline_result: MAE 2.9° / RMSE 6.9° for Cobb angle (vs 5.4°/12.5° single-task baseline); R=0.96 vs radiographic measurement
40913670.study_design: Retrospective model development and evaluation study

40937462.clinical_problem: Quantifying fetal brain cortical expansion and growth via deformable image registration for developmental studies
40937462.model_description: Physics-informed deep learning registration method (using neural ODEs and growth/remodeling mechanics); one of several applications aligns longitudinal fetal brain MRI to quantify cortical expansion during development (also applied to adult brain atrophy and zebrafish fin regrowth).
40937462.study_design: Methods development study with benchmark comparisons across multiple non-clinical and clinical datasets

40939270.exclusion_reason: Radiation dose survey establishing national diagnostic reference levels for pediatric head CT; no AI/ML model (deep learning reconstruction mentioned only as a future practice recommendation).

40960398.clinical_problem: Generating missing infant brain MRI time points to study early brain developmental trajectories
40960398.patient_population: Infants from the Baby Connectome Project
40960398.model_description: Three-stage age- and modality-conditioned deep learning framework takes existing T1/T2-weighted infant brain MRI scans as input and synthesizes brain MRI at missing longitudinal time points, also performing tissue segmentation and cortical reconstruction.
40960398.dataset_size: 848 MRI scans from 139 infants (119 training, 20 test)
40960398.headline_result: SSIM 0.87-0.90 (T1), 0.87-0.89 (T2); Dice 0.85 gray matter, 0.86 white matter segmentation

40967651.exclusion_reason: Study protocol for validating WHO childhood-TB treatment decision algorithms; AI-interpreted radiology is listed as one of several 'novel tools' to be evaluated in future work, not a developed or evaluated model in this record.

40972662.exclusion_reason: Segmentation network for fetoscopic surgical video (placental vessel visualization during laser surgery for TTTS); fetoscopy is direct endoscopic/optical visualization, not radiologic imaging, and the method is evaluated across multiple unrelated general medical imaging datasets.

40985603.clinical_problem: Predicting which neonates with hydrocephalus will need CSF diversion surgery, using MRI and clinical data
40985603.patient_population: Neonates with suspected raised intracranial pressure/hydrocephalus, including myelomeningocele and post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus
40985603.model_description: Combines multimodal MRI features with clinical data to predict, at the individual-neonate level, future need for CSF diversion (shunt or ETV).
40985603.dataset_size: 116 neonates (development cohort, China); 21 neonates (external validation cohort, USA)
40985603.headline_result: AUC 0.824 development cohort (vs 0.528 clinical-only, 0.685 imaging-only); AUC 0.808 external validation cohort
40985603.study_design: Retrospective model development with external validation

40992502.clinical_problem: Automatically measuring fetal biometry (head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length) and estimating fetal weight from ultrasound
40992502.patient_population: Pregnant patients with healthy fetuses undergoing routine ultrasound
40992502.model_description: Classifies ultrasound video frames into standard fetal biometry planes (HC/AC/FL), then automatically measures each parameter; fetal weight estimated via the Hadlock 3 formula.
40992502.dataset_size: 16,626 training images; prospective validation on 281 ultrasound videos
40992502.headline_result: Mean absolute error vs expert: 0.96% HC, 1.56% AC, 1.77% FL, 3.10% fetal weight

40993183.clinical_problem: Detecting pathologies and identifying medical device placement on neonatal radiographs in the NICU
40993183.patient_population: Infants admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit (4,629 infants, Boston, 2008-2023)
40993183.model_description: Self-supervised contrastive-learning foundation model trained on neonatal radiographs paired with radiology reports; detects 15 radiological features and 5 medical devices.
40993183.headline_result: Higher AUROC than controls for all labels except portal venous gas
40993183.study_design: Retrospective model development and internal validation

40996509.exclusion_reason: Systematic review/meta-analysis of AI for ACL tear diagnosis on MRI in the general population; not specific to pediatric radiology, children mentioned only as context for rising injury rates.

41063006.clinical_problem: Predicting postnatal neurodevelopmental outcome in monochorionic twins using fetal brain MRI radiomic features
41063006.model_description: Extracts radiomic texture features from fetal brain MRI regions; a logistic regression model with nested cross-validation predicts postnatal neurodevelopmental outcome (good vs moderate).
41063006.dataset_size: 26 monochorionic twin pregnancies, 36 fetuses (20 good, 16 moderate neurodevelopmental outcome)
41063006.headline_result: Mean AUC 0.89 (±0.11) for predicting neurodevelopmental outcome
41063006.study_design: Retrospective cohort study with radiomics-based prediction model

41089184.exclusion_reason: Prediction of epilepsy/neurodevelopmental outcome in neonatal HIE uses EEG signals and clinical data as the ML inputs; MRI is used only for a manual Barkovich injury score, not as AI model input.

41110031.clinical_problem: Diagnosing, monitoring, and predicting outcomes in early onset scoliosis (children under 10) using AI
41110031.patient_population: Children with early onset scoliosis (younger than 10 years)
41110031.model_description: Scoping review of 11 studies applying AI/ML (mostly CNNs such as Mask R-CNN, EfficientNet, U-Net) to automate radiographic measurements (Cobb angle, skeletal maturity), monitor growing-rod distraction, and predict complications/reoperation in early onset scoliosis.

41188293.clinical_problem: Automatically detecting wrist fractures on pediatric radiographs
41188293.patient_population: Children with wrist injuries (GRAZPEDWRI-DX public dataset)
41188293.model_description: Takes pediatric wrist radiographs as input and outputs bounding-box fracture detections, using an improved YOLO11s architecture (C3k2-WTConv module, Focaler-MPDIoU loss) with a GUI-based diagnostic tool.
41188293.dataset_size: GRAZPEDWRI-DX public dataset of pediatric wrist radiographs
41188293.headline_result: vs YOLO11 baseline: +3.2% precision, +1.6% recall, +1.8% mAP@50, +3.2% mAP@50-95

41206361.body_region: thorax and abdomen (lungs, kidneys, liver, spleen, skin boundary)
41206361.clinical_problem: Automatically segmenting thoraco-abdominal organs on dynamic MRI to support surgical planning in children with thoracic insufficiency syndrome and scoliosis
41206361.patient_population: 189 (near-)normal children/pediatric subjects, including healthy children and patients with thoracic insufficiency syndrome
41206361.model_description: Two-stage deep learning pipeline (DL-R for recognition, DL-D for delineation) takes dynamic MRI slices at different respiratory phases as input and outputs segmentations of the lungs, kidneys, liver, spleen, and thoraco-abdominal skin boundary.
41206361.dataset_size: 189 subjects (dynamic MRI); 89 training, 10 validation, 90 test at end-inspiration/expiration
41206361.headline_result: Dice 0.92-0.94 lungs, 0.82 kidneys, 0.90 liver, 0.81 spleen, 0.93 skin boundary
41206361.study_design: Retrospective model development and evaluation study

41231298.model_family: large language model (Llama-3.1-8B with retrieval-augmented generation)
41231298.body_region: not specified (general pediatric imaging appropriateness across clinical scenarios)
41231298.clinical_problem: Recommending the appropriate imaging modality for pediatric clinical scenarios per ACR Appropriateness Criteria
41231298.patient_population: not stated (50 simulated pediatric clinical scenarios, not real patients)
41231298.model_description: A retrieval-augmented-generation chatbot built on a locally deployed open-source LLM (Llama-3.1-8B) takes a pediatric clinical scenario as input and outputs an ACR Appropriateness Criteria-concordant imaging modality recommendation.
41231298.dataset_size: 50 pediatric clinical scenarios derived from ACR guideline variants
41231298.headline_result: ped-Llama 80% 'usually appropriate' accuracy (90% including 'may be appropriate') vs 46-54% for generic LLMs, matching specialist radiologist (76%); run-to-run consistency 72% vs 44-50%

41231299.body_region: peripheral limbs (hand/wrist, elbow, shoulder, knee/leg, foot/ankle)
41231299.clinical_problem: Detecting fractures (and, for one algorithm, joint effusions/dislocations) on radiographs of children with limb trauma in the emergency department
41231299.patient_population: 366 children under 18 referred by the pediatric emergency department for radiographic exploration of limb trauma
41231299.model_description: Two commercially available AI algorithms analyze plain radiographs of pediatric peripheral limb trauma to flag fractures (and, for Boneview, effusions/dislocations), evaluated standalone and as a second reader for radiology residents.
41231299.release_evidence: two commercially available AI software programs (Boneview and Rayvolve)
41231299.headline_result: Boneview sensitivity 0.85/specificity 0.87 (AUC 0.862); Rayvolve sensitivity 0.81/specificity 0.93 (AUC 0.874); AI significantly improved junior resident performance

41266569.clinical_problem: Estimating fetal gestational age from any ultrasound image or video without requiring dedicated biometry planes
41266569.patient_population: 78,531 pregnancies (Australia, India, UK); independent validation on 742 fetuses
41266569.model_description: Deep learning model takes any fetal ultrasound image or video, regardless of orientation, as input and outputs a gestational age estimate with an image-quality-based uncertainty value.
41266569.dataset_size: over 2 million ultrasound images from 78,531 pregnancies; independent validation on 36,762 images from 742 fetuses
41266569.headline_result: MAE 1.7 days (14-18 weeks), 2.8 days (18-24 weeks); video MAE below 3 days across all trimesters, outperforming traditional biometry
41266569.study_design: Retrospective model development with independent multi-country validation

41286495.exclusion_reason: Catalog and quality scoring of public ultrasound datasets and open-source models across all anatomies; not a pediatric-focused study (notes a gap in fetal ultrasound datasets but is not itself pediatric radiology AI research).

41291881.exclusion_reason: Adult female IBS patients; 'adverse childhood experiences' refers to participants' past history, not a pediatric imaging study; brain MRI is performed in adults.

41296212.clinical_problem: Assessing bone age and predicting adult height from pediatric hand radiographs to evaluate growth
41296212.model_description: Cascaded deep learning framework: Yolact detects and classifies hand bone structures, parallel ResNet-18 subnetworks grade ossification centers in the radius, ulna, and metacarpal/phalangeal bones, a scoring system estimates bone age, and a regression model predicts adult height.
41296212.headline_result: Pearson r 0.98 (bone age), 0.94 (adult height); MAE 0.25 years bone age, 1.75 cm adult height

41300634.exclusion_reason: Pediatric dental imaging (panoramic radiograph diagnosis of furcation lesions in primary molars); dental imaging is out of scope.

41300905.clinical_problem: Detecting fractures on pediatric elbow radiographs in the acute emergency setting
41300905.patient_population: 200 pediatric elbow radiographs (100 normal, 100 abnormal) from a tertiary pediatric hospital
41300905.model_description: General-purpose multimodal LLM (ChatGPT-4o) is prompted with anonymized pediatric elbow radiographs via a standardized prompt and outputs a fracture vs. no-fracture prediction and fracture site.
41300905.headline_result: Accuracy 85%, sensitivity 87%, specificity 82%, F1 0.85, Cohen's kappa 0.69 vs. ground-truth reports

41306444.model_family: deep transfer learning + radiomics + machine learning classifier
41306444.clinical_problem: Differentiating complicated from uncomplicated appendicitis in children using ultrasound and laboratory data
41306444.patient_population: 372 pathologically confirmed pediatric appendicitis cases (230 male, 142 female) from three centers
41306444.model_description: Combines deep-transfer-learning image features and radiomic features from appendiceal ultrasound images with clinical lab values (WBC, neutrophils, CRP) in a machine learning classifier to distinguish complicated from uncomplicated appendicitis.
41306444.headline_result: Combined model AUC 0.940/0.895/0.866/0.783 across cohorts; accuracy 0.862, comparable to senior surgeons and superior to junior surgeons
41306444.study_design: Retrospective multi-center model development and validation

41320594.clinical_problem: Detecting pediatric fractures on musculoskeletal radiographs and improving radiologist accuracy
41320594.patient_population: 3016 pediatric MSK radiographs from 4 US imaging centers (Phase 1); 189 cases read by 20 readers (Phase 2 MRMC)
41320594.model_description: Deep learning AI model analyzes pediatric musculoskeletal radiographs to flag fractures; evaluated standalone and as a second-reader aid for radiologists in a multi-reader, multi-center study.
41320594.headline_result: Standalone accuracy 0.94, sensitivity 0.96, specificity 0.86; with AI assistance reader accuracy 0.93->0.96, sensitivity 0.86->0.93; reading time -26.1%
41320594.study_design: Multicenter retrospective standalone evaluation plus multi-reader multi-center study

41389104.clinical_problem: Measuring Cobb angle on preoperative whole-spine radiographs in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, including severe and extreme curves
41389104.patient_population: 151 preoperative anteroposterior whole-spine radiographs from surgical AIS cases
41389104.model_description: Commercially available deep learning software automatically measures Cobb angle from preoperative whole-spine radiographs; compared against pediatric radiologist/orthopedic surgeon consensus ground truth and radiology residents.
41389104.dataset_size: 151 preoperative whole-spine radiographs (13 moderate, 74 severe, 64 extreme curves)
41389104.headline_result: AI MAE 4.57 deg (95%CI 3.85-5.29), ICC 0.89 vs ground truth; MAE significantly higher than residents, especially for extreme scoliosis (6.53 vs 3.61 deg)

41393720.exclusion_reason: Review explicitly restricted to adult human imaging by the authors' own inclusion criteria; pediatric and animal studies were excluded from this review.

41452364.clinical_problem: How to ethically develop, validate, and deploy AI models on pediatric imaging data
41452364.model_description: Review discussing ethical strategies for AI development and deployment in pediatric radiology, covering regulatory hurdles, bias mitigation, human oversight, and interdisciplinary collaboration among developers, clinicians, and families.

38177034.clinical_problem: Establishing normal reference values for global and layer-specific myocardial strain in healthy children and young adults using AI-based cardiac MRI strain analysis
38177034.patient_population: 131 healthy children and young adults (62 male, 69 female; mean age 16.6+/-3.9 years)
38177034.model_description: TrufiStrain deformable-registration research prototype software analyzes cine cardiac MRI to automatically compute global and layer-specific (endocardial-to-epicardial) myocardial strain values (longitudinal, radial, circumferential).
38177034.headline_result: Peak global longitudinal strain -16.0+/-3.0%, radial strain 29.9+/-6.3%, circumferential strain -17.0+/-1.8%

38266713.body_region: brain (right inferior frontal gyrus functional connectivity)
38266713.clinical_problem: Identifying brain connectivity patterns linking harsh/unpredictable childhood environments to binge eating tendencies in late adolescents
38266713.patient_population: 501 late adolescents aged 16-22 (376 completed an additional attentional-bias task)
38266713.model_description: Linear support vector regression with leave-one-out cross-validation is applied to resting-state fMRI dynamic functional connectivity features (right inferior frontal gyrus connectivity) to test the robustness of the brain-behavior association between childhood environmental harshness and binge eating tendencies.
38266713.dataset_size: 501 late adolescents (376 with attentional-bias task data)
38266713.study_design: Cross-sectional neuroimaging study with machine-learning robustness check

38269595.clinical_problem: Predicting white matter injury in premature infants from cranial ultrasound and monitoring its recovery over time
38269595.model_description: Radiomics features extracted from five standard cranial ultrasound planes are combined via a LASSO-selected signature into a multiplanar model that predicts white matter injury and tracks its recovery on serial scans.

38277712.exclusion_reason: Standard group-level fMRI analysis of developmental grammar learning; no AI/machine-learning model is used.

38304541.clinical_problem: Diagnosing and differentiating bacterial pneumonia from other pneumonia types on chest radiographs
38304541.patient_population: 10 included studies; 126,610 images and 1,706 patients spanning children and adults
38304541.model_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis pooling ten studies of deep learning models that identify bacterial pneumonia (versus viral/fungal) on chest X-rays/radiographs in children and adults.

38321311.model_family: radiomics + machine learning classifiers (logistic regression, SVM, neural network, AdaBoost)
38321311.clinical_problem: Screening for T-cell lymphoma subtype in children with lymphoma using 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics
38321311.patient_population: Children with lymphoma undergoing FDG PET/CT (77 patients / 247 lesions in training set)
38321311.model_description: Radiomics features from PET/CT images (SUV-based and combined PET/CT features) are used with several machine learning classifiers, with logistic regression performing best, to screen for T-cell lymphoma subtype in pediatric lymphoma patients.
38321311.dataset_size: 77 patients / 247 lesions (training set); separate validation set
38321311.headline_result: Best (logistic regression, PET/CT model): accuracy 0.779-0.838, AUC 0.863-0.907 (patient and lesion level)

38336117.clinical_problem: Determining fetal sex from ultrasound images
38336117.patient_population: 19,212 ultrasound image slices from a high-volume fetal sex determination practice
38336117.model_description: A computer vision model (EfficientNetB4 via transfer learning) classifies fetal ultrasound images into male, female, unable-to-assess, or text-added categories to determine fetal sex.
38336117.headline_result: Accuracy 88.27%, Cohen's kappa 0.843; AUC 0.896-0.981 across classes

38343234.clinical_problem: Segmenting the fetal head and measuring head circumference from ultrasound to assess fetal growth
38343234.patient_population: not stated (public HC18 fetal head ultrasound dataset)
38343234.model_description: Deep learning model (hierarchical density regression CNN incorporating appearance and shape priors) segments the fetal head in ultrasound images and estimates head circumference via robust ellipse fitting.
38343234.headline_result: Dice 98.86%; absolute distance error 1.67 mm; correlation coefficient 0.99 for head circumference
38343234.study_design: Retrospective model development study on a public benchmark dataset

38349519.exclusion_reason: Bibliometric systematic review of gender trends in pediatric radiology authorship; an AI tool (genderize.io) is used only as a methodological aid to infer author gender, not as the subject of the review.

38366768.clinical_problem: Diagnosing foreign body aspiration in children from chest radiographs
38366768.patient_population: 566 pediatric patients with suspected foreign body aspiration, 2010-2020
38366768.model_description: A machine learning algorithm trained with Google AutoML Vision analyzes frontal chest radiographs to flag foreign body aspiration, compared against pediatric radiologist interpretation.
38366768.headline_result: Algorithm sensitivity 66.7%, specificity 95.3% (vs radiologist 50.6%/88.7%); precision/recall 91.8%, AuPRC 98.3%

38382423.clinical_problem: Assessing structural and functional cardiac changes (myocardial non-compaction) in neonates born to preeclampsia/eclampsia-affected pregnancies using echocardiographic radiomics
38382423.patient_population: 2,594 neonates screened; 556 selected for detailed radiomics analysis
38382423.model_description: Radiomics features (cardiac shape, movement, texture) extracted from neonatal echocardiograms are integrated with a multiblock sparse partial least squares model to identify imaging signatures associated with maternal preeclampsia/eclampsia exposure.
38382423.dataset_size: 2,594 neonates screened; 556 in radiomics analysis; 15,494 features extracted per neonate
38382423.headline_result: sPLS identified 17 features correlated with PE/E; strongest texture feature r=0.63; LVEF 61.1% vs 66.2% in controls
38382423.study_design: Retrospective cohort study with radiomics analysis

38402375.model_family: machine learning (classification and regression models, algorithm unspecified)
38402375.clinical_problem: Identifying brain structural and connectivity correlates of emotion regulation ability in children at high risk for autism spectrum disorder
38402375.patient_population: 55 children at high risk of autism spectrum disorder, 52 typically developing children
38402375.model_description: Machine learning classification and regression models relate structural MRI/diffusion tensor imaging-derived white matter fiber bundle connectivity and amygdala/hippocampus volumes to emotion regulation behaviors in children at high risk of autism spectrum disorder.
38402375.dataset_size: 55 high-risk ASD children, 52 typically developing children
38402375.headline_result: R2 0.245 (right amygdala volume) and 0.667 (white matter connectivity predicting mother-seeking behavior) for emotion regulation strategies
38402375.study_design: Retrospective case-control neuroimaging study with machine learning models

38415463.clinical_problem: Automatically measuring scoliosis Cobb angle on spine radiographs
38415463.patient_population: 481 spine radiographs (open-source dataset, train/validation) and 119 spine radiographs from a private dataset (test), pediatric and adolescent scoliosis patients
38415463.model_description: Two deep learning Cobb angle assessment models (Seg4Reg, a segmentation-based regression model, and VFLDN, a keypoint-based landmark detection model) automatically measure spinal curvature on radiographs, compared against manual physician measurement.
38415463.dataset_size: 481 spine radiographs (open dataset, train/validation); 119 radiographs (private dataset, test)
38415463.headline_result: VFLDN: ICC 0.974, PCC 0.952 vs manual (MAD 2.36 deg); Seg4Reg: ICC 0.809, PCC 0.731 (MAD 6.51 deg)
38415463.study_design: Retrospective external validation and clinical application study

38426209.clinical_problem: Automating bone age assessment for Han and Tibetan children, including in resource-limited high-altitude settings
38426209.patient_population: RSNA and RHPE public datasets plus a local Han/Tibetan children dataset (825 train, 351 test: 216 Han, 135 Tibetan); external test set of 256 Tibetan children
38426209.model_description: EVG-BANet, a deep learning bone age assessment model trained on RSNA and RHPE datasets plus a local Han/Tibetan children dataset, is compared against the open-source BoNet model across multiple test sets including an external all-Tibetan cohort.
38426209.dataset_size: RSNA (12,611/1,425/200 train/val/test); RHPE (5,491/713/79); local dataset (825 train, 351 test); external Tibetan test set (n=256)
38426209.headline_result: MAD 0.52-0.53 years (RHPE, external Tibetan test sets) vs BoNet 0.63-0.66 years; accuracy within 1 year 97.7% local, 89.5% external
38426209.study_design: Retrospective model development with external validation

38490997.exclusion_reason: Animal (rhesus monkey) study of infant temperament and brain metabolism; not a human pediatric radiology study.

38522222.clinical_problem: Detecting polymicrogyria, a subtle cortical malformation, on pediatric brain MRI
38522222.patient_population: Children with polymicrogyria and controls from the Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario (PPMR dataset)
38522222.model_description: A center-based deep contrastive metric learning anomaly-detection method flags pediatric brain MRIs likely to show polymicrogyria, intended as a computer-aided screening tool for radiologists; code and a new open pediatric MRI dataset (PPMR) are released publicly.
38522222.release_evidence: Our code is available at: https://github.com/RichardChangCA/... ; dataset available at kaggle.com/datasets/lingfengzhang/pediatric-polymicrogyria-mri-dataset
38522222.dataset_size: Small, imbalanced pediatric MRI dataset (PPMR; exact N not stated in abstract)
38522222.study_design: Retrospective model development study, first ML application to detect polymicrogyria from MRI

38605540.exclusion_reason: Phantom-based contrast-media dose-reduction study for CT (adult and pediatric size phantoms); deep learning reconstruction is used as one of two reconstruction techniques compared, incidental to the primary iodine-CNR optimization methodology, and no clinical patients are studied.

38653568.model_family: radiomics + multivariate logistic regression / random forest
38653568.clinical_problem: Predicting which neuroblastic tumors are high-risk neuroblastoma using MRI radiomics
38653568.patient_population: 32 patients (training, institution A) and 14 patients (external test, institution B), age <=18 years
38653568.model_description: Radiomics features (n=930) extracted from manually segmented pre-treatment MRI tumor regions feed multivariate logistic regression and random forest models (10-fold cross-validated) that predict high-risk neuroblastoma status; models were tested on an external institution's cohort.
38653568.headline_result: MLR model AUC 0.94 training and test; random forest AUC 0.83 (training CV), 0.91 (test)
38653568.study_design: Retrospective pilot study with external test set

38672556.clinical_problem: Differentiating medulloblastoma from pilocytic astrocytoma, the two most common pediatric brain tumors, preoperatively
38672556.patient_population: 195 preoperative MRIs from children with medulloblastoma (n=69) or pilocytic astrocytoma (n=126) across six university hospitals
38672556.model_description: A patch-based 3D-DenseNet deep learning classifier, using automated tumor segmentation and all individually available preoperative MRI sequences, differentiates medulloblastoma from pilocytic astrocytoma and is compared against five human readers of varying experience.
38672556.dataset_size: 195 preoperative MRIs (69 medulloblastoma, 126 pilocytic astrocytoma) from six university hospitals; 64-patient test set
38672556.headline_result: AUC 0.986; 62/64 (97%) correct diagnoses in test set; on par with pediatric neuro-oncology experts, better than inexperienced readers (p<0.05)
38672556.study_design: Retrospective multicenter proof-of-concept diagnostic accuracy study

38704285.model_family: machine learning (AdaBoost, KNN, SVM with SHAP explainability)
38704285.clinical_problem: Differentiating early-onset schizophrenia from early-onset bipolar disorder using brain MRI surface morphometry
38704285.patient_population: 144 adolescents (mean age 16.2+/-1.4 years): 81 with early-onset schizophrenia, 63 with early-onset bipolar disorder
38704285.model_description: Explainable machine learning classifiers (AdaBoost, KNN, SVM) using T1-weighted MRI-derived cortical thickness, gyrification, sulcal depth, fractal dimension, and brain volume features, interpreted via SHAP, differentiate early-onset schizophrenia from early-onset bipolar disorder.
38704285.headline_result: AdaBoost accuracy 82.75% (Destrieux atlas, all variables); KNN accuracy 79.31% (Desikan-Killiany-Tourville atlas)

38730032.clinical_problem: Predicting postnatal enlarged lateral ventricle outcomes in fetuses with isolated ventriculomegaly from a single prenatal MRI
38730032.patient_population: 141 normal fetuses, 101 fetuses with ventriculomegaly (68 resolved, 33 stable), 2014-2023
38730032.model_description: Logistic regression models (5-fold cross-validated) using lateral ventricle morphology and cortical/subcortical radiomics features from a single fetal MRI predict postnatal lateral ventricle alterations in fetuses with isolated ventriculomegaly.
38730032.headline_result: Subcortical-radiomics model distinguishing normal vs ventriculomegaly fetuses: AUC 1/0.992 (train/val); predicting postnatal alteration: AUC 0.822/0.743 (train/val)

38766538.clinical_problem: Segmenting the fetal head on ultrasound for prenatal biometric measurement
38766538.patient_population: not stated (described as the largest dataset to date for fetal head metrics)
38766538.model_description: FetSAM is a prompt-based deep learning segmentation model for fetal head ultrasound images, using a dual loss (weighted Dice + weighted Lovasz) and benchmarked against U-Net, DeepLabV3, and Segformer.
38766538.dataset_size: Largest fetal head ultrasound dataset to date (exact N not stated)
38766538.headline_result: Dice 0.90117, Hausdorff distance 1.86484, average surface distance 0.46645
38766538.study_design: Retrospective model development and benchmarking study

38772798.clinical_problem: Predicting macrolide-resistance-associated gene mutation status in children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia from chest CT
38772798.patient_population: 258 pediatric MPP patients (194 training at institution 1, 64 external test at institution 2)
38772798.model_description: Radiomics features from semi-automatically segmented pulmonary lesions on chest CT are used in logistic regression and random forest models to predict 23S rRNA gene mutation status (macrolide resistance) in children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
38772798.dataset_size: 258 patients (194 training, 64 external test), two institutions
38772798.headline_result: Logistic regression AUC 0.868 (train), 0.855 (external test); random forest AUC 0.941 (train), 0.815 (external test)
38772798.study_design: Retrospective two-center model development and external validation study

38781934.clinical_problem: Detecting congenital heart defects on fetal ultrasound to improve early detection rates beyond the current ~60%
38781934.model_description: Review of deep-learning-based fetal ultrasound image evaluation techniques (preprocessing, localization, segmentation, classification, including CNN-based denoising and CNN/ANN-based segmentation) for detecting congenital heart defects.

38786405.clinical_problem: Detecting wrist fractures in children from infrared thermal imaging as an alternative/adjunct to X-ray
38786405.patient_population: 40 participants (19 with wrist fracture, 21 with sprain), diagnosis confirmed by X-ray
38786405.model_description: A 34-layer CNN classifies Fourier-transformed infrared thermal images of pediatric wrists (frequency-domain magnitude spectra) as fractured or non-fractured (sprain).
38786405.study_design: Retrospective pilot diagnostic model development study

38797384.exclusion_reason: Non-human primate (macaque, chimpanzee, marmoset, etc.) brain MRI processing toolbox; not a human pediatric radiology study.

38802611.clinical_problem: Assessing bone age in preschool children and reducing inter/intra-observer variability with AI assistance
38802611.patient_population: 94 preschool children aged 3-6 years (53 female, 41 male), China
38802611.model_description: An AI model system assists radiology reviewers performing bone age assessment (TW3 and RUS-CHN methods) on hand radiographs of preschool children; evaluated for its effect on inter- and intra-observer agreement rather than as a standalone diagnostic tool.
38802611.headline_result: ICC values exceeded 0.99 with AI assistance; RMSE/MAE significantly decreased with AI (p<0.001)
38802611.study_design: Retrospective reader study on observer variability with AI assistance

38831994.clinical_problem: Distinguishing children from adults with Mycoplasma pneumonia based on clinical, CT imaging, and radiomic features, and quantitatively representing CT imaging signs
38831994.patient_population: 981 Mycoplasma pneumonia patients (590 internal: 450 adults/140 children; 391 external test: 121 adults/270 children)
38831994.model_description: Combined clinical, CT-image, and radiomics (LASSO-selected from 1,904 extracted features) logistic regression models differentiate adult from pediatric Mycoplasma pneumonia cases and provide quantitative radiomic representations of qualitative CT signs.
38831994.study_design: Retrospective multi-cohort model development and external validation

38832703.clinical_problem: Predicting risk of scoliosis curve progression in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis based on bone microarchitecture phenotypes
38832703.patient_population: Primary cohort n=101 girls with AIS (followed 6.22+/-0.33 years); secondary cohort n=106 girls with mild AIS
38832703.model_description: Unsupervised machine learning (fuzzy C-means clustering) groups girls with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis into three bone microarchitecture phenotypes based on HR-pQCT parameters, which are then tested as predictors of curve-progression risk to surgical threshold.
38832703.dataset_size: Primary cohort n=101; secondary cohort n=106
38832703.headline_result: Phenotype 3: OR 4.88 (95%CI 1.03-28.63) for progression to surgical threshold; secondary cohort OR 5.39 (phenotype 2), 3.67 (phenotype 3) for progression >=6 degrees
38832703.study_design: Prospective longitudinal cohort study with unsupervised ML phenotyping

38841427.exclusion_reason: General-population MRI contrast-enhancement generative model (GAN); pregnant women and children are mentioned only as populations that could benefit from reduced contrast-agent use, not as the actual study population (dataset/cohort not described as pediatric).

38842257.exclusion_reason: Serum metabolomics study of pediatric Crohn disease inflammation; MR enterography is used only to define outcome measures (the PICMI index), not as AI model input, and the machine learning (random forest) model predicts from serum metabolite biomarkers, not from imaging.

38873982.clinical_problem: Assessing feasibility of automated fetal cardiac functional analysis (2D speckle-tracking echocardiography) for less experienced operators
38873982.patient_population: 136 normal singleton second- and third-trimester fetuses
38873982.model_description: FetalHQ, a semi-automated two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography tool, calculates fetal cardiac functional and morphometric parameters (strain, fractional shortening, sphericity index) from ultrasound; compared between beginner and expert operators.
38873982.headline_result: Excellent inter-operator agreement for morphometry (ED, SI), good agreement for function (endoGLS, FS); Bland-Altman bias -4.24pp/-3.21pp for endoGLS

38899013.exclusion_reason: Automated classification of lung auscultation sounds (audio signals, not imaging) using deep learning; not a radiology imaging modality.

38902015.exclusion_reason: Standard fMRI group analysis of body image/self-concept development in adolescents; no AI/machine-learning imaging model is used.

38926172.clinical_problem: Automatically reconstructing 3D spine anatomy and measuring curvature parameters (Cobb angle, vertebral rotation, kyphosis, lordosis) from biplanar radiographs in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
38926172.patient_population: 380 paired biplanar (EOS) radiographs of children with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (304 pairs training, 76 pairs test)
38926172.model_description: An AI algorithm reconstructs a 3D scoliotic spine from paired posteroanterior and lateral EOS biplanar radiographs and automatically extracts curvature parameters (Cobb angle, apical vertebral rotation, kyphotic and lordotic angles), compared against manual measurement by an experienced rater.
38926172.headline_result: MAD 3.3 deg (Cobb angle), 1.5 deg (vertebral rotation), 3.3 deg (kyphotic angle), 3.5 deg (lordotic angle); 98% within clinical acceptance; ICC >0.94; reconstruction in 5.2+/-1.3s

38937304.clinical_problem: Differentiating benign from malignant, and among four etiologies of, cervical lymphadenopathy in children using MRI radiomics
38937304.patient_population: 419 cervical lymph nodes from 146 pediatric patients
38937304.model_description: Radiomic features (1,218 per lymph node) extracted from T2-weighted MRI, reduced via LASSO, feed support vector machine classifiers to distinguish benign from malignant cervical lymph nodes and to differentiate among four common etiologies (Kikuchi disease, reactive hyperplasia, suppurative lymphadenitis, malignancy).
38937304.dataset_size: 419 lymph nodes from 146 patients (7:3 train/test split)
38937304.headline_result: Benign vs malignant AUC 0.89 (train), 0.80 (test); four-etiology model AUC 0.87-0.97 (train), 0.80-0.96 (test)

38976189.exclusion_reason: Pneumonia classification model from chest X-rays; children are mentioned only as one at-risk population in the introduction, and the study population/dataset is not stated to be pediatric.

38991771.clinical_problem: Detecting skull fractures and evaluating cranial suture patency without ionizing radiation, using deep-learning pseudo-CT generated from MRI in children
38991771.patient_population: 72 patients younger than 18 (12 for suture patency evaluation, 60 for head trauma evaluation)
38991771.model_description: Automated motion correction is applied to MR imaging, followed by a deep-learning method that generates pseudo-CT images of the pediatric skull from MRI, evaluated for skull fracture detection and cranial suture patency assessment against ground-truth CT.
38991771.dataset_size: 72 patients (12 for suture patency, 60 for head trauma)
38991771.headline_result: Suture patency: 100% sensitivity/specificity; skull fracture detection: 100% specificity, 90% sensitivity

39018640.model_family: deep learning (knowledge distillation + contrastive regularization, scribble-supervised segmentation)
39018640.clinical_problem: Reducing annotation cost for placenta and fetal brain segmentation on fetal MRI using scribble (weak) annotations instead of full pixel-level labels
39018640.patient_population: not stated (fetal MRI dataset used as one of two benchmarks, alongside an adult cardiac MRI dataset)
39018640.model_description: ScribSD+ is a scribble-supervised segmentation framework (multi-scale knowledge distillation plus class-wise contrastive regularization) that learns to segment the placenta and fetal brain on fetal MRI (and cardiac structures on adult cardiac MRI) from scribble annotations instead of full pixel-level labels.
39018640.headline_result: Outperformed five state-of-the-art scribble-supervised segmentation methods (fetal-MRI-specific Dice not given in abstract)
39018640.study_design: Retrospective methods development and benchmarking study

39060444.clinical_problem: Forensic bone age assessment (determining whether a person is above or below legal age thresholds of 12/14/16/18) from hand and wrist MRI in Chinese Han males
39060444.model_description: A deep learning model extracts and enhances epiphyseal features from hand and wrist MRI to classify subjects into legal age categories (12/14/16/18-year thresholds) and regress a continuous bone age estimate.
39060444.headline_result: Adult vs minor classification accuracy 91.1%; minor age-threshold classification accuracy 91.1-96.4%; regression MAE 1.24 years

39098096.exclusion_reason: Development of a manual, visual semiquantitative myelination scoring system for pediatric MRI; not an AI/ML model itself (deep learning approaches are mentioned only as background/related work).

39112675.model_family: deep learning (accelerated Turbo Spin Echo reconstruction)
39112675.clinical_problem: Evaluating diagnostic performance and image quality of deep-learning-accelerated MRI in children and young adults with knee/ankle symptoms
39112675.patient_population: 48 subjects, 49 MRIs (10 males, mean age 16.4 years, range 7-29 years)
39112675.model_description: Deep-learning image reconstruction accelerates Turbo Spin Echo MRI sequences of the knee and ankle, evaluated for diagnostic accuracy and image quality against conventional sequences and, when available, arthroscopy.
39112675.headline_result: Sensitivity/specificity vs conventional: knees 90.7%/99.3%, ankles 100%/100%; DL sequences 2x faster acquisition

39125510.clinical_problem: Diagnosing pediatric thoracic diseases from chest X-rays using models pretrained on adult data (knowledge transfer), given limited pediatric training data
39125510.patient_population: Pediatric CXR dataset (PhysioNet); population not otherwise detailed
39125510.model_description: A three-stage self-supervised and transfer-learning framework fine-tunes transformer (ViT) and CNN models, pretrained on adult chest X-ray datasets (e.g., CheXpert), to diagnose and localize six pediatric thoracic disease categories on a small pediatric chest X-ray dataset.
39125510.release_evidence: The source code is available online and the data can be obtained from PhysioNet.
39125510.dataset_size: Pediatric CXR dataset (PhysioNet); size not stated
39125510.headline_result: ViT-Base/16 fine-tuned on CheXpert: mean AUC 0.761 (95%CI 0.759-0.763) across 6 disease categories, sensitivity 0.639, specificity 0.683
39125510.study_design: Retrospective model development and benchmarking study

39133952.model_name: ADU-GD (Attention Gate Double U-Net with Guided Decoder)
39133952.clinical_problem: Segmenting and measuring fetal biometric parameters (head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length, biparietal diameter) from ultrasound
39133952.model_description: ADU-GD, an attention-gated double U-Net with a guided decoder, segments fetal anatomical structures on ultrasound and estimates biometric parameters (head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length, biparietal diameter), benchmarked against numerous other deep-learning segmentation models.
39133952.headline_result: MAE 0.99 mm overall; Dice 99.1%; parameter MAE: HC 2.2mm, AC 2.6mm, FL 0.6mm, BPD 1.2mm
39133952.study_design: Retrospective model development and benchmarking study

39144940.model_family: k-nearest neighbor, SVM, random forest, XGBoost
39144940.body_region: fetal (prenatal screening, combined with biochemical markers)
39144940.clinical_problem: Screening for Down syndrome in the first and second trimesters using ultrasound and biochemical testing, especially in resource-limited settings
39144940.patient_population: 7,076 pregnant women in Northern Vietnam (1,035 with a fetus with Down syndrome)
39144940.model_description: Machine learning models (k-nearest neighbor, SVM, random forest, XGBoost) combine ultrasound findings and biochemical test results to predict Down syndrome risk in the first and second trimesters.
39144940.dataset_size: 7,076 pregnant women, single site in Northern Vietnam
39144940.headline_result: Trimester 1: XGBoost 94% accuracy, 88% AUC; Trimester 2: SVM 89% accuracy, 84% AUC

39186484.clinical_problem: Improving image quality of pediatric cardiac CT while managing radiation dose, comparing deep-learning reconstruction to conventional iterative reconstruction
39186484.model_description: Deep learning image reconstruction (TrueFidelity, at low/medium/high strength settings) is compared to adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction for quantitative (SNR, CNR, sharpness) and qualitative image quality on pediatric cardiac CT.
39186484.headline_result: High-level DLIR significantly improved SNR and CNR vs ASiR-V (P<0.05); improved sharpness (edge rise distance)

39256496.exclusion_reason: Animal (rat) model study of placental dysfunction in preeclampsia; not a human pediatric or fetal study.

39263285.model_family: CNN (DenseNet121 best of AlexNet, VGG16, Inception v3, ResNet50, DenseNet121)
39263285.clinical_problem: Diagnosing adenoid hypertrophy causing upper airway obstruction in children from lateral nasopharyngeal radiographs
39263285.patient_population: 1,188 children aged 8 months to 13 years (mean 5.57+/-2.66 years), three hospitals
39263285.model_description: Five deep learning models (AlexNet, VGG16, Inception v3, ResNet50, DenseNet121) are trained to diagnose adenoid hypertrophy from lateral nasopharyngeal radiographs; the best model (DenseNet121) is compared against three radiologists of varying seniority.
39263285.dataset_size: 1,188 children, three hospitals; 208 images in internal validation group
39263285.headline_result: DenseNet121 AUC 0.892 internal / 0.872 external; accuracy 0.895/0.878; comparable to senior radiologist (0.892 vs 0.901, p=0.79)
39263285.study_design: Retrospective multicenter model development with internal and external validation

39271408.body_region: cervix (maternal, for prenatal preterm-birth risk assessment)
39271408.clinical_problem: Automating region-of-interest selection for quantitative ultrasound analysis of the cervix to predict spontaneous preterm birth risk
39271408.model_description: A deep learning model automatically determines the field of interest for quantitative ultrasound (QUS) analysis of the cervix from B-mode ultrasound images, intended to replace time-consuming manual delineation for real-time preterm-birth risk assessment.
39271408.headline_result: Pixel accuracy 97%, Dice coefficient 87%; Pearson r=0.87 for attenuation coefficient vs manual field of interest

39284691.exclusion_reason: Study protocol for a cohort study relating preterm birth to neurodevelopment and cognition; no AI/ML model is described (planned analysis uses multivariable regressions and structural equation modeling).

39288819.exclusion_reason: Machine learning model predicting maternal surgical morbidity in placenta accreta spectrum; predominantly uses demographic and obstetric variables, with prenatal imaging findings only a minor input among 213 variables. Not a radiology-imaging-focused study.

39326551.exclusion_reason: Scoping review of critical-findings classification/communication standards in emergency radiology; the review's own inclusion criteria explicitly omit resources with an explicit pediatric focus or a predominant AI/NLP focus.

39385257.clinical_problem: Predicting cardiomyopathy risk in childhood cancer survivors from serial echocardiograms
39385257.patient_population: At-risk childhood cancer survivors >=1 year post initial cancer therapy, five centers; 542 pairs of echocardiogram montages (45 cases, 70 non-case survivors)
39385257.model_description: Deep convolutional neural networks trained on serial echocardiogram image montages, from multiple time points relative to cardiomyopathy diagnosis, predict which childhood cancer survivors are approaching or have developed cancer-therapy-related cardiomyopathy.
39385257.dataset_size: 542 pairs of echocardiogram montages (171 from 45 cases, 371 from 70 non-case survivors), five centers
39385257.headline_result: AUROC 0.89+/-0.02, AUPRC 0.83+/-0.03, F1 0.76+/-0.04 distinguishing case vs non-case montages
39385257.study_design: Retrospective multicenter model development study (10-fold cross-validation)

39395303.model_family: deep learning (dual dilated attention + multi-scale deformable transformer + graph convolution attention)
39395303.clinical_problem: Segmenting fetal brain tissue on MRI to support assessment of normal and congenital-disease-affected fetal neurodevelopment
39395303.patient_population: not stated (FeTA 2021 and FeTA 2022 public fetal brain MRI datasets)
39395303.model_description: MG-Net is a deep learning segmentation model, combining a dual dilated attention block, a multi-scale deformable transformer, and a graph convolution attention decoder, that automatically segments fetal brain tissue on MRI; code is released publicly.
39395303.release_evidence: The code is available at https://github.com/unicoco7/MG-Net/
39395303.headline_result: FeTA 2021: Dice 0.8666, IoU 0.7646, MAE 0.0027; FeTA 2022: Dice 0.8552, IoU 0.7470, MAE 0.0005; outperformed nnFormer, SwinUNETR, 3DUX-net
39395303.study_design: Retrospective model development and benchmarking study on public datasets

39396080.exclusion_reason: Animal (mouse) study of blood-biomarker-based radiation biodosimetry; not human, and not an imaging study (uses blood cell/protein biomarkers via flow cytometry, not radiology images).

39432664.exclusion_reason: Review of prediction models for endometriosis-associated ovarian carcinoma in adult women; not pediatric, and predictors are largely serological/clinical rather than radiology-image-based.

39433994.exclusion_reason: Logistic regression model predicting preterm birth from maternal socio-demographic and obstetric history; explicitly avoids using imaging (cervical length ultrasound) as an input.

39447089.exclusion_reason: Machine learning model predicting pediatric Hodgkin lymphoma treatment response from blood test results, not imaging; PET-CT findings are the prediction target/reference rather than a model input.

39509989.exclusion_reason: Standard fMRI functional connectivity analysis comparing adolescents with autism spectrum disorder to typically developing peers during a language task; no AI/machine-learning model is used.

39539491.exclusion_reason: Pilot fMRI study of neurofeedback-augmented mindfulness training in typically developing adolescents; uses standard statistical (linear mixed effects) analysis, not an AI/machine-learning model.

39546640.clinical_problem: Suppressing bone structures on pediatric chest radiographs to reduce missed pneumonia diagnoses caused by bone occlusion
39546640.patient_population: Customized pediatric CXR dataset (P260): 40 labeled images for fine-tuning, 220 unlabeled images for testing; network pretrained on 240 adult CXR images
39546640.model_description: A deep learning bone-suppression network, pretrained on adult chest radiographs and fine-tuned via an efficient automated labeling pipeline (distance-transform-based bone-edge detection plus traditional image processing), generates separate bone and soft-tissue images from pediatric chest radiographs without specialized dual-energy equipment.
39546640.dataset_size: 240 adult CXR (pretraining); 40 labeled + 220 unlabeled pediatric CXR (P260 dataset)
39546640.headline_result: Bone-suppression network: relative MAE 3.38%, PSNR 35.5 dB, SSIM 98.1%, bone-suppression ratio 90.1%

39568996.exclusion_reason: Transformer-based deep learning model predicting acute hematogenous osteomyelitis and blood culture results from laboratory indicators; radiology is mentioned only as background context, not used as a model input.

39616218.clinical_problem: Predicting subcortical (thalamic) functional connectivity from cortical fNIRS signals for potential bedside brain monitoring, including in neonates with early brain injury
39616218.patient_population: Healthy adults and neonates with early brain injuries (two separate datasets)
39616218.model_description: A graph convolutional network predicts cortical-thalamic functional connectivity, as measured by fMRI, from cortical functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) data, evaluated in healthy adults and separately in neonates with early brain injury, as a step toward using fNIRS for bedside brain monitoring of critically ill patients.
39616218.dataset_size: Two datasets: healthy adults and neonates with early brain injury (sample sizes not stated in abstract)
39616218.headline_result: GCN outperformed SVM and feedforward artificial neural networks for both binary connection classification and connection-strength regression
39616218.study_design: Retrospective model development and benchmarking study

39673623.clinical_problem: Predicting postoperative brain development / neurocognitive outcome in children treated for hydrocephalus, using brain and ventricular volumes and MRI texture
39673623.patient_population: 52 children under age 10 undergoing hydrocephalus treatment
39673623.model_description: Three deep-learning classification models use texture information from pre- and postoperative T1-weighted brain MRI to predict brain development outcomes in children treated for hydrocephalus, compared using four-fold cross-validation.
39673623.headline_result: Accuracy 0.808 for postoperative-image-based prediction of brain development
39673623.study_design: Retrospective cohort study with deep learning prediction models

39685997.clinical_problem: Generating synthetic CT from cone-beam CT for adaptive proton and carbon-ion radiotherapy planning in pediatric oncology patients
39685997.model_description: An unsupervised CycleGAN-based model generates synthetic CT images from cone-beam CT scans of pediatric pelvic patients, intended to support image-guided adaptive proton and carbon-ion particle therapy without an additional planning CT.
39685997.dataset_size: 15 young pelvic patients, 44 CBCT scans (36 training, 8 testing volumes)
39685997.headline_result: Improved SSIM and PSNR of synthetic CT vs verification CT compared to raw registered CBCT (quantitative and qualitative improvement)

39689732.clinical_problem: Characterizing white matter (diffusion MRI) abnormalities in pediatric bipolar disorder, including whether machine learning classifiers can differentiate patients from healthy controls
39689732.patient_population: 23 included studies of children/adolescents with pediatric bipolar disorder vs. healthy controls
39689732.model_description: Systematic review of 23 diffusion MRI studies in pediatric bipolar disorder, synthesizing white matter tract abnormalities (fractional anisotropy, diffusivity, structural connectivity) and noting that machine learning classifiers built on these diffusion MRI features showed promising ability to differentiate pediatric bipolar disorder from healthy controls.

39700855.clinical_problem: Generating synthetic 3D brain tumor MRI regions to address class imbalance in tumor genetic-marker/type classification, including pediatric low-grade glioma BRAF V600E mutation status
39700855.patient_population: BraTS 2019 low-grade glioma cases (public, largely adult) and an internal pediatric low-grade glioma (pLGG) dataset
39700855.model_description: A vector-quantization GAN combined with a transformer (masked token modeling) generates high-resolution, diverse synthetic 3D brain tumor regions of interest on MRI, used to augment imbalanced training data for tumor-type/genetic-marker classification, including BRAF V600E mutation status in pediatric low-grade glioma.
39700855.dataset_size: BraTS 2019 low-grade glioma cases (public); internal pediatric low-grade glioma dataset
39700855.headline_result: Augmentation improved classification AUC by 6.4% (BraTS 2019) and 4.3% (internal pLGG dataset)
39700855.study_design: Retrospective model development study using public and internal datasets

39708564.exclusion_reason: Machine learning model (PBIPred) predicting preterm brain injury from clinical/laboratory variables (mechanical ventilation, weight, anemia of prematurity, respiratory distress syndrome, albumin, white blood cell count); cranial MRI is used only to define the outcome label, not as a model input.

39711742.clinical_problem: Diagnosing and assessing severity of pediatric pneumonia even when some data modalities (imaging or clinical text) are missing
39711742.patient_population: Pediatric pneumonia patients (a new comprehensive pediatric pneumonia multimodal dataset was developed; N not stated in abstract)
39711742.model_description: The Robust Multimodal Transformer (RMT) integrates chest X-ray images and clinical text via a transformer architecture with multi-task learning and a mask attention mechanism, diagnosing and grading pediatric pneumonia severity robustly even when one modality (image or text) is missing.
39711742.dataset_size: not stated (new pediatric pneumonia multimodal dataset developed for this study)
39711742.headline_result: Outperformed traditional diagnostic methods and baseline models in accuracy, precision, sensitivity, and specificity (exact figures not given in abstract)

39717438.clinical_problem: Automating skull-stripping and tumor segmentation for monitoring pediatric brain tumors, including rare sellar/suprasellar tumors, in limited-data scenarios with missing MRI sequences
39717438.patient_population: 527 pediatric patients (336 for skull-stripping, 489 for tumor segmentation) with various pediatric brain tumor histologies, multi-institutional (Children's Brain Tumor Network)
39717438.model_description: Separate nnU-Net-based deep learning models perform skull-stripping (including sellar/suprasellar regions) and whole-tumor / enhancing-tumor segmentation on multi-institutional, multi-parametric pediatric brain tumor MRI, robust to single or multiple input sequences and missing data.
39717438.dataset_size: 527 pediatric patients (336 skull-stripping, 489 tumor segmentation), multi-institutional (CBTN)
39717438.headline_result: Skull-stripping Dice 0.98+/-0.01; whole tumor Dice 0.84+/-0.17 (T2) / 0.82+/-0.19 (FLAIR); enhancing tumor Dice 0.65+/-0.35 (T1-Gd+FLAIR)

39723659.clinical_problem: Predicting fetal birthweight from ultrasound data, including classifying appropriate-, large-, and small-for-gestational-age status
39723659.model_description: A deep learning model combining feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), a gated recurrent unit (GRU), and an attention network processes sequential maternal and fetal ultrasound parameters to predict fetal birthweight and classify appropriate-, large-, and small-for-gestational-age status.
39723659.headline_result: Prediction accuracy 98.8%, outperforming ensemble transfer learning (83.5%), BabyNet++ (91.7%), and other baselines
39723659.study_design: Retrospective model development and benchmarking study
